Comcast today launched Xfinity Shield, a new home security platform that includes a feature that turns the router into a motion sensor. Here are the details.

Xfinity Shield is a new security platform that includes "WiFi Motion" for motion detection.

Home security has historically focused on physical threats like break-ins, but today it also covers cyber threats. Comcast's launch of the new Xfinity Shield platform aims to protect users in both areas.

Details about Xfinity Shield can be found in the press release, but one point particularly worth noting is that it can turn users' existing home routers into motion sensors.

Not every Xfinity router supports the motion sensing feature, but a good number of models do. According to the official support page, this opt-in feature works with the Technicolor XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10.

However, there is one privacy concern worth noting. According to TechCrunch, the page also states: "To the extent permitted by applicable law, Comcast may disclose information generated by your WiFi Motion to third parties without further notice to you, including in connection with any law enforcement investigation or legal proceeding, any dispute to which Comcast is a party, or pursuant to a court order or subpoena."

The good news is that, for example, motion data will not be sold to third-party advertisers. However, if you have any privacy concerns, you can simply choose not to enable the WiFi Motion feature.

Would you use the new motion sensing feature on your Xfinity router? Let us know in the comments.
